fills.reason: Looked for external-storage APIs (getExternal*, MediaStore) and WRITE/MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE: none. Files go to filesDir/cacheDir; the CSV export writes to a user-chosen SAF document via CreateDocument.
No SecretKeySpec or key bytes in code; all AES keys are generated inside AndroidKeyStore. The Mixpanel project token is an analytics ID, not a crypto key.
No android.util.Log, println or printStackTrace calls in app or sync. OkHttp's HttpLoggingInterceptor is added only when BuildConfig.DEBUG, at BASIC level, and redacts the Authorization header.
The only WebView (HelpActivity) enables JavaScript but explicitly sets allowContentAccess = false and never enables universal access from file URLs.
HelpActivity sets allowFileAccess = false and doesn't enable file-URL or universal access, so the fail combination isn't met.

The password uses OutlinedSecureTextField, but the 'Private note' field (which the app encrypts at rest with a Keystore key, so treats as sensitive) is a plain OutlinedTextField with the default caching/autocorrecting keyboard.

evidence.detail: Private note field uses a plain OutlinedTextField with no non-caching KeyboardOptions (autoCorrect off / password type).

fills.reason: No FLAG_SECURE (or any screen-capture prevention) anywhere, yet MainActivity shows financial data: expenses, amounts, places and decrypted private notes.

evidence.detail: MainActivity sets its content without ever setting WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE on the window.

fills.reason: Searched app and sync for Notification/NotificationCompat builders and POST_NOTIFICATIONS: the app posts no notifications.
The only access-code field (password on LoginScreen) is an OutlinedSecureTextField with the default obfuscation mode, never set to Visible.
HelpBridge is exposed with JS enabled, but its methods only return the app version and close the activity (nothing sensitive), and navigation is limited to https://help.pennyjar.example.

The login screen and settings (biometric unlock, delete account) have no filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, obscured-flag checks or setHideOverlayWindows, though the app targets API 36.

evidence.detail: Sign-in button submitting credentials has no overlay/tapjacking protection.

fills.reason: The internal HelpActivity launch is explicit (Intent(context, HelpActivity::class.java)). The only implicit intents are user-facing ACTION_VIEW to a browser and ACTION_SEND through a chooser.

Implicit intents with extras are ACTION_SEND share flows wrapped in Intent.createChooser (the share link and a receipt image the user chose to share). There are no tokens or credentials in implicit extras.
Searched app and sync for PendingIntent.getActivity/getService/getBroadcast: the app creates no PendingIntents.
The only deep-link intent-filter uses the custom scheme pennyjar://help; no http/https App Links are declared.

HelpActivity reads the 'page' query parameter and loads it in the WebView only if the scheme is https and the host equals help.pennyjar.example. Anything else goes to the external browser only for http/https.
This test needs a real backup and restore with bmgr. The static rules are judged under MASTG-TEST-0262.

Both rule files exclude credentials.xml, session.xml and unlock.xml (email, encrypted session token, biometric secret) from cloud backup and device transfer. Expense data (receipts.db, receipt photos, backup CSV) is still backed up, which looks like a deliberate choice for user data; notes in it are Keystore-encrypted.

The only exported non-launcher activity, HelpActivity, shows public help pages from one allowlisted https host. It reads no user data, does no security-relevant action, and doesn't skip the login or biometric lock in MainActivity.
kotlin.random.Random is only used to pick an avatar colour from the merchant name. Security values (share-link token, biometric secret) use SecureRandom, and IVs come from the Cipher.
No time-based or other non-random source feeds a security value. Tokens and secrets use SecureRandom, photo file names use UUID.randomUUID.
The only key generation (KeystoreKeys.create) uses AES with setKeySize(256). There are no RSA/EC keys.
Every Cipher.getInstance uses AES/GCM/NoPadding. No DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish.
All transformations are AES/GCM/NoPadding. No ECB or bare "AES".
The app calls BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(BIOMETRIC_STRONG) before enabling or using biometric unlock, an accepted way to detect a secure lock screen.
No KeyPairGenerator or asymmetric keys. The only Keystore keys are AES keys with ENCRYPT|DECRYPT.
The only named provider is AndroidKeyStore (KeyStore.getInstance and KeyGenerator.getInstance for Keystore keys). Cipher.getInstance uses the default provider.
BiometricPrompt allows only BIOMETRIC_STRONG. DEVICE_CREDENTIAL and setDeviceCredentialAllowed aren't used.
BiometricPrompt.authenticate gets a CryptoObject, and the key is created with setUserAuthenticationRequired(true). Unlock depends on decrypting the sealed secret with the authenticated cipher.
The biometric key is created with setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(true).
PromptInfo never calls setConfirmationRequired(false), so explicit confirmation stays on (the default).
The biometric key uses setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG) on API 30+ and setUserAuthenticationValidityDurationSeconds(-1) below, so every use needs authentication.
Neither OkHttpClient builder sets ConnectionSpec or tlsVersions. No SSLContext.getInstance or setEnabledProtocols, so platform TLS defaults apply.
The only http:// URL is the debug buildType's API_BASE_URL (10.0.2.2 emulator host). Release uses https://api.pennyjar.example/, and the other endpoints are https constants.
Searched app and sync for SSLSocket/SSLSocketFactory: none. All traffic goes through OkHttp, which verifies hostnames.
No custom X509TrustManager or checkServerTrusted anywhere. OkHttp uses the platform trust manager and the NSC trusts system CAs only.
No custom HostnameVerifier is set on either OkHttpClient, and no code calls verify().
HelpActivity's WebViewClient overrides only shouldOverrideUrlLoading, not onReceivedSslError, so SSL errors cancel by default.

The app never calls ProviderInstaller and has no Google Play services dependency (see libs.versions.toml). Decide whether to add play-services-basement and update the provider before networking, or accept the platform Conscrypt on minSdk 26.
The NSC has no pin-set for any domain, and neither OkHttpClient sets a CertificatePinner, so API, upload, image and help hosts are unpinned (relevant for MASVS-NETWORK-2 / L2).

evidence.detail: base-config trusts system CAs with no pin-set and there's no domain-config with pins.

fills.reason: No code calls WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled.
shouldOverrideUrlLoading allows in-WebView navigation only when the scheme is https and the host exactly equals help.pennyjar.example. Other URLs go to the browser.
No EnableSafeBrowsing=false meta-data in the manifests and no setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false) in HelpActivity.
The app checks Build.VERSION.SDK_INT against VERSION_CODES.R to choose the stronger key-authentication API.
No Play In-App Updates API and no backend minimum-version check. BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME is only exposed to the help page, and startup goes straight to session restore.

evidence.detail: Startup navigation picks Login/Locked/home with no update-enforcement check first.

The project has no native code: no .so/.c/.cpp files, CMake or ndkBuild config.

The biometric_unlock boolean is read from plain SharedPreferences with no HMAC or signature, and it alone decides whether MainActivity shows the Locked screen. Flipping it to false skips the biometric lock.

evidence.detail: Biometric-lock flag read from SharedPreferences without integrity verification.
The unverified flag decides whether the app is locked behind biometrics.

The project has no native binaries (no .so files or native build config).
No root detection anywhere: no su/Magisk path checks, build-tag checks, root-detection library or Play Integrity call.

evidence.detail: Server user ID sent to Mixpanel via identify().
Expense category and amount band sent to Mixpanel.
